title: Sequential Room Unlocking via Key Acquisition
description:
There are 'n' rooms, indexed from 0 to n-1. Initially, only Room 0 is unlocked, and all other rooms are locked. You are currently in Room 0.

Inside each room, you may find a set of keys. Each key is labeled with the number of the room it unlocks. You can collect all keys found in any room you enter and use them to unlock and enter subsequent rooms. You can visit the rooms in any order, provided you have the necessary key.

Your task is to determine if it is possible to visit every single room.
input_format: The first line contains an integer n (the number of rooms). Then n lines follow, representing rooms 0 to n-1. Each line starts with an integer k (the number of keys in that room), followed by k space-separated integers representing the labels of the rooms those keys unlock.
output_format: Print 'true' if you can visit all n rooms, otherwise print 'false'.
constraints:
2 <= n <= 1000
Total keys <= 3000
0 <= key label < n
